We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 3 reactions using templates 1914393, 1914394, 1914395 in this order.

We have applied template 1914393 to target SMILES, got precursors: ('COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1'). So first disconnection yields two fragments: fragment A = COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nn[nH]c2N)c1 (the aromatic part with amide and triazine? Actually nnn). fragment B = FC1CN(Cc2ccc(CCl)cc2)C1 (a fluorinated azetidine? Actually a fluoromethyl? It's a fluorinated piperidine? Anyway.)

Now we need to apply template 1914394 to each fragment? The order is 1914393 then 1914394 then 1914395. Likely we apply 1914394 to fragment A or B, then 1914395 to resulting fragment(s). We attempted applying 1914394 to fragment A (COc1... ) got no result. Apply to fragment B gave result: ('ClCCl', 'FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1'). So template 1914394 splits fragment B into two: a dichloromethane? Actually ClCCl (dichloromethane) and FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1 (a fluorinated N-heterocycle attached to phenyl). So second step: fragment B -> precursors: dichloromethane (ClCCl) and FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1.

Now we need to apply template 1914395 to the remaining fragment(s). Likely to the FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1 to replace F with OH? The template 1914395 is a transformation: [F]-[CH]1-[C]-[#7]-[C]-1 >> O-[CH]1-[C]-[#7]-[C]-1 (retro). So it converts a fluorine attached to a carbon in a heterocycle to OH. So applying to FC1CN(Cc2ccccc2)C1 should give O... product: OCH1... So we apply 1914395 to that fragment.

Let's do that.
